hints.title: Interpret sufficiency
hints.body: For each proposed condition, ask whether every polynomial satisfying it must have a real zero. One polynomial satisfying the condition but missing all real zeros disproves sufficiency.
hints.pitfall: The three statements are not assumed together.
hints.pause: Consider the two tails of a cubic with nonzero leading coefficient.

recall.reminder: Sufficiency means the condition alone guarantees the target.

hints.title: Distinguish a stationary point from a root
hints.body: To test the stationary-point condition, try a vertical translation of a quadratic with a stationary point. Consider whether you can position its graph so the derivative vanishes somewhere while the graph never meets the horizontal axis.
hints.recap: A counterexample must satisfy the stated premise and fail the claimed conclusion.
hints.pitfall: A zero derivative is not a zero function value.
hints.pause: Choose an explicit quadratic and verify both its derivative condition and its minimum before judging the statement.

recall.reminder: A derivative gives gradient; a function value gives height. Check these separately when testing a claimed implication.

hints.title: Analyse the two sign conditions
hints.body: Translate <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> into the possible signs of the two values. Separately examine the signs of a nonzero cubic’s leading term at the two ends of the real line.
hints.recap: A polynomial graph is continuous between any two inputs.
hints.pitfall: Use the polynomial assumption when reasoning from opposite signs to an axis crossing.
hints.pause: Determine whether each remaining condition guarantees an axis crossing and combine all three verdicts.

recall.reminder: A polynomial graph is continuous between any two inputs.

solution:
I is sufficient: with nonzero cubic coefficient, the leading term gives opposite signs for sufficiently large positive and negative x. A polynomial is continuous, so it must pass through zero.

II is not sufficient: f(x)=x2+1 has f′(0)=0 but f(x)>0 everywhere, so it has no real zero.

III is sufficient: f(u)f(v)<0 means the endpoint values have opposite signs. By continuity, a real zero lies between u and v.

Answer C: Yes, No, Yes.
knowledgePattern: Use continuity and odd degree to guarantee a zero
